title: TROIKA: a general framework for heart rate monitoring using wrist-type photoplethysmographic signals during intensive physical exercise
authors: Zhang Z, Pi Z, Liu B
population: 12 subjects running fast, up to a peak speed of 15 km/h, wearing a wrist-type PPG device with a reference heart rate
findings: Wrist-type PPG signals during intensive exercise are contaminated by extremely strong motion artifacts caused by the subjects' hand movements.

The TROIKA framework (signal decomposition for denoising, sparse signal reconstruction for a high-resolution spectrum, spectral peak tracking with verification) gave an average absolute error of 2.34 beats per minute on the 12 subjects running at up to 15 km/h, with a Pearson correlation of 0.992 against the ground-truth heart rate.
limitations: An algorithm paper on 12 subjects, using raw PPG and accelerometer signals; the abstract does not describe a check that can be run on a watch's already-processed heart rate, and says nothing about hills or about a particular device's firmware.
implications: Motion artifact is the named error source of wrist PPG in running, and detecting and verifying the heart-rate peak is how research algorithms handle it; this supports a data-quality check on stored heart rate, not any threshold.
The thresholds of the HQ1 checks are design choices; no study validates them on stored 10 s streams.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 62(2):522-531, February 2015, authors Zhang, Pi, Liu. Abstract read in Europe PMC (PMID 25252274); the numbers are copied from it. Design recorded as modelling: an algorithm evaluated on a small dataset.
